messages:
pagerduty-bot: INC1850123 - Alert: runtime/gpu OOM rate > 20% on prod-inference cluster for model: redwood-v1. Paging @Devon (on-call).

Devon: on it, ack. Any recent deploys or config changes?

infra-bot: Auto-detected anomaly: request qps steady, but per-GPU OOMs spiked ~17:04 UTC. Link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/oom-spike (screenshot attached).

Ajay: I’m on the GPU fleet. Pulling logs now. Which pool is affected?

Devon: pool=prod-gpu-1, model=redwood-v1-quant, routing=default. Impacting 4/12 nodes in that pool. Customers: some high qps PLG users saw 502s.

Kevin: I’m checking the runtime traces — seeing a bunch of errors like:

```
E runtime: kv_cache.cpp:432 allocate_prefix_kv_cache: CUDA error: out of memory
Trace: rtx_allocate(sizeof=1.2G) failed
```

Kevin: Also continuous-batcher logs show a burst that pushed batch sizes from median 3 -> 10 for ~30s around the spike.

Devon: ok hypothesis 1: sudden batch-size growth + heavy prefix KV cache allocations -> fragmentation/alloc failures. Hypothesis 2: a single large request bypassed prefix size checks and starved GPU memory.

Michelle: short-term mitigation suggestions: 1) reduce max_batch_size to 4 on prod-gpu-1, 2) temporarily disable prefix KV caching for redwood-v1-quant, 3) force-evict large KV pages after 30s. I can apply 1 & 2 as a canary.

Devon: do it. Post the exact commands here so SRE runbook shows what happened.

Michelle: running patch now.

```
# reduce batch size for pool prod-gpu-1
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.internal/api/runtime/configs/apply \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}' \
  -d '{"pool":"prod-gpu-1","max_batch_size":4}'

# disable prefix kv cache for specific model
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.internal/api/runtime/models/redwood-v1-quant/config \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}' \
  -d '{"kv_cache": {"enabled": false, "eviction_ms": 30000}}'
```

Michelle: confirmed change applied to 2 nodes as canary (node ids: gpu-1-05, gpu-1-06).

Ajay: running restart of serving process on the two canary nodes to pick up config.

Ajay: post-restart telemetry: error rate on canary nodes dropped from 18% -> 1.2% in 120s. CPU and GPU utilization normalized.

Devon: good. Roll changes to rest of pool with staged rollout (50% -> 100%) and monitor.

Kevin: in parallel I pulled nvidia-smi dumps from affected hosts. snippet:

```
# nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY -i 0
FB Memory Usage
    Total                       : 40536 MiB
    Used                        : 38910 MiB
    Free                        : 1626 MiB
CUDA Version: 12.1
Fragmentation ratio (API-est): 0.81
```

Kevin: Also capturing allocator debug from runtime:

```
alloc_stats: total_allocated=38.9G peak=39.5G free_frag=1.2G fragmented_chunks=23
kv_cache: active_pages=512 active_bytes=9.6G
continuous_batcher: current_max=10 observed_peaks=14
```

Michelle: that fragmentation ratio and the small free region explains the OOMs even though total free seems non-zero. When allocs require contiguous blocks >1G they fail.

Devon: tagging this as prod-oom-frag. We should also check if quantization changes earlier this week modified allocator behavior. Kevin, can you fetch model binary build id + recent compile flags?

Kevin: pulling build id: redwood-v1-quant@2026-03-10-13:22. Compile flags include fast-kernel=on and arena_prealloc=off. Comparing to stable build, arena_prealloc used to be on. Could be related.

Ajay: I can quickly run a node-local repro by replaying large prefix traffic against a test node with arena_prealloc=false and high batch sizes. If it reproduces, we get a smoking gun.

Devon: please do that and post logs. Also, collect full GDB/malloc dump from one of the crashed processes (if available) and upload to S3.

Ajay: started replay job, will take ~12 minutes to ramp. Link to logs: https://s3.redwood.internal/oom-repro/1850123456/ajay-run-1.log

Michelle: meanwhile, quick note on customer impact: we throttled routing for tier=free to reduce pressure at 17:09, which dropped qps by ~25% for the pool. Enterprise customers on dedicated capacity not impacted. Noting those affected for the postmortem.

Devon: handoff: I need to drop off in 20m. Michelle, you're primary for the remainder of the live MITIGATION and RCA coordination. I'll leave escalation to Ajay/Kevin if the canary rollback fails.

Michelle: ack, I'll take over. @Ajay please DM any raw dumps and point me to the S3 path.

Ajay: repro finished. Observed OOM at ~7th iteration when batch peaked at 12. Pasted error and stack:

```
E runtime: allocator.cpp:211 defragment: cannot coalesce, largest_free_chunk=768MB, requested=1.2GB
E runtime: model_infer: failed to allocate KV Page size=1.2GB
```

Ajay: uploaded gdb/minidumps to s3://redwood-debug/ooms/1850123456/{gpu-1-09,gpu-1-11}.tar.gz

Michelle: good evidence. Hypothesis A (confirmed): arena_prealloc=false + bursty batching -> fragmentation -> large contiguous alloc fails. Hypothesis B (less likely): a single oversized request without proper validation.

Kevin: action item: revert arena_prealloc to true for redwood-v1-quant build and schedule a new compile with fragmentation mitigations (e.g., slab pre-warming). I can run a canary build tomorrow.

Michelle: action item: add runtime guard to reject model requests that would request KV pages > 512MB unless explicitly whitelisted. Also add telemetry to track contiguous allocation size requirements.

Devon: also add cluster-level policy: cap continuous-batcher max to 6 when kv_cache.enabled=true. That’s an operational lever to avoid this class of regression.

Ajay: noted. Creating tickets: INF-4721 (revert arena_prealloc), INF-4722 (runtime guard + telemetry), INF-4723 (batcher cap policy). I’ll attach reproducer logs.

Michelle: rolling summary for postmortem thread: initial trigger = burst in batch size -> allocator fragmentation on quantized model -> contiguous KV page allocation failed -> OOMs and request failures; short-term fix = reduced batch size + disable kv_cache for model -> error rate fell. Long-term = compile flag change, runtime guards, batcher caps.

Devon: excellent. tagging product + support: please prepare customer communication for affected PLG users; include that dedicated customers were unaffected.

Michelle: will draft a quick status and push to #customer-impact and #postmortems. Will also paste timeline and attach allocator logs.

Kevin: final runtime note: set of nodes with highest fragmentation were older GPU drivers (driver 525.x) vs others on 535.x. Driver interplay possible but lower priority. Adding to INF-4724 for driver validation.

Devon: thanks all. I’m switching to follow-up mode. Michelle — you have the incident.

Michelle: taking incident to stabilize + RCA writeup. If anyone finds additional repro variants, drop them into this thread or upload to the S3 path. :thumbsup:

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC1850123 status changed: acknowledged -> mitigation in progress.

Michelle: updating last_message_ts before I close the live coordination: 1850123570. Follow-ups will be in #postmortems.

Kevin: leaving a couple of quick diagnostic commands for the RCA doc:

```
# per-host fragmentation and cuda mem stats
nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY; grep -i fragment alloc_logs.txt | tail -n 100
# dump allocator map
/opt/redwood/bin/allocator-dump --out /tmp/alloc-map.json
```

Ajay: uploaded final repro logs and annotated stack traces to s3://redwood-debug/oom-repro/1850123456/final/

Michelle: closing live mitigation thread. Moving to postmortem drafting. :white_check_mark:
